items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: Man, he called me up for a parade. I think we must have walked up about 40 miles.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. My grandpa used to play, but I don't think he was in the union. I don't think he was in the union. Jules, Jules, yeah. Jules, yeah, but my uncle. He's there, he's a play ball. Yeah, I don't think. He's a play ball. He's a play ball to us. Yeah. What was his name? No, he wasn't. Jules, Jules, Jules. Jules, Jules. Jules, Jules. I remember the time Jules. I remember that name from somewhere. Well, Mom. We've become a Jules. Is he living yet? Yeah, he's in Florida. From the same way. Yeah, Jules, Jules,…

Is he still around? Yeah, on the magazine street. What is that Italian holiday that they paraded over there? Oh, it's in St. Rosalie. St. Rosalie. St. Rosalie. Man, he called me up for a parade. I think we must have walked up about 40 miles. He can't?
Yeah. Well, old man, Carazard, used to play in the band. Uncle Joe, too, used to play.
